summary: Zhihua Yao works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel (~1996-2002), and held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2003) and The University of Hong Kong (2005).

Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed an MA at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and a PhD at the University of Arizona under doctoral supervisor Robert M. Gimello.

Zhiru Shi is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello, having also studied under Donald Harper, Beth Harrison, and Alan E. Bernstein, and served at Pomona College (attested 2007-2014).

Zhiyi Yang is a sinologist who studied at Peking University, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, and Princeton University (PhD under Martin Kern). Her posts include assistant researcher at Erlangen-Nürnberg and an affiliation at Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed an MA at SOAS University of London and a PhD at The University of Hong Kong, where she later served as a teaching consultant (attested 2013).
Zhongpei Zhang was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied under Su Bai (~1952-1956). He later served as director of the Palace Museum (~1987-1991).

Zhongxin Jiang worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960-1965), later holding posts at Peking University (~1968-1978), the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978-2002), and Soka University (~1999).
Zhuan Dao was a Buddhist studies figure who studied as a student under Tongzhi. He later founded Poo Thor Jee in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.
Zijie Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 2015) and held a post as a DC research fellow with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2015).
Zoltán Gombocz was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Evangélikus Líceum until 1895 and at Eötvös Loránd University from 1895 to 1900.

Zong Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Ganden Shartse Monastery (-1929) and Gyuto Monastery (1929) under mentors including Trijang Rinpoche. He served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse (1937-1946) and director/rector at CIHTS (1965, 1967-1971).

Zongsan Mou was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University (1927-1933) under Shili Xiong. He taught across several universities before holding major posts at CUHK (~1968-1974) and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (~1974-1995).

Zsóka Gelle is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Vienna. She has held posts at Dharma Gate Buddhist College, the University of Vienna (2011-2014), and ELTE (2014-2016).
Zuicho Tachibana was a researcher in history/archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kōzui Ōtani (~1903) and Edward Denison Ross (~1910-1912).

Zuiei Ito specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo. He was a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (1980-2013) and also lectured at Tokyo, Waseda, and Shinshu Universities.

Zuigan Goto was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Sōkatsu Shaku (~1900-1914) and attended the Second Higher School and the University of Tokyo (1903-1906). He served as president of Hanazono University in 1932.

Zuiho Yamaguchi worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After degrees at the University of Tokyo and EPHE under Jacques Bacot and Rolf A. Stein, he held posts at CNRS, Toyo Bunko (1964-1970), Tokyo University (1970-1986), and Nagoya University (1986).

Zuiryu Nakamura was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi in 1944. He became a professor at Rissho University in 1945 and served as director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.
Gyurme tubten nyinje studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Pad+ma la studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Rinpoche.
